title: The Big 5 of Inequality — TikTok
notes: Hook question: why can one bad month push an American family into poverty? Answer, scene by scene: five forces (housing, healthcare, education, incomes, jobs) decide who gets ahead, each is under strain, and they are linked, so one shock spreads to the rest. Each section ends on its 'interconnected' link from the article, which leads into the next force. The close: fix them together, not one at a time.

All figures are from the article (Nov 4, 2026) and the sources it cites (Harvard JCHS, KFF, NAEP, Opportunity Insights, Federal Reserve, NY Fed, Desmond and Gershenson). Solo post, so the narration uses 'I'.
VOICE: ElevenLabs, generated only after the author approves the script. Render drafts with the default --voice keep.

post.headline: The 5 forces that decide who gets ahead
post.caption: Housing, healthcare, education, incomes and jobs decide whether an American family gets ahead, and none of them works alone. A record 22.7 million renters are cost burdened, family health premiums hit $26,993, and losing a job often means losing your coverage too.
post.cta: Full story and interactive charts at the link in bio.

scenes.source: The Big 5 of Inequality · American Inequality
say: In America, one bad month can knock a family into poverty.

scenes.source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies
say: A record 22.7 million renters now spend more than 30% of their income on rent.
I call these the Big 5 forces of inequality, and when one breaks, the others follow.

scenes.source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies
say: Housing comes first. Renters earning under $30,000 had a record-low $210 a month left after rent and utilities.

scenes.title: Median home price vs. median household income
scenes.source: The Big 5 of Inequality · American Inequality
say: Owning is harder too, since a median home cost 2.5 times the median income in 1989, and 5 times today.

overlays.label: homeless students, the most on record

say: And losing a home follows kids to school, where a record 1.5 million students were homeless last year.

scenes.title: Growth from 2014 to 2024
say: Healthcare is next. Family premiums now average $26,993 a year, and they grew 52% in a decade while inflation rose 32%.
When enhanced ACA subsidies expired, marketplace enrollment fell for the first time in years, by about 3 million people.
Education is slipping, as 13-year-olds gained 21 points in math from 1978 to 2012, then lost 15 of them by 2025.

scenes.title: Share of the nation's wealth, 2026
say: Incomes hit a record in 2025, but the top 1% now hold 32.5% of the nation's wealth while the bottom half holds just 2.5%.
That makes the climb steeper, since 92% of kids born in 1940 out-earned their parents, compared with half of those born in 1980.

scenes.source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
say: Jobs are the last force, and recent college grads now face higher unemployment than the average worker.

overlays.label: of Americans get health insurance through work

scenes.source: The Big 5 of Inequality · American Inequality
say: And since 53.5% of Americans get health insurance through work, losing a job often means losing your coverage, and then your rent.
Affordability was the top issue for voters this year, because families feel all five forces at once.
We can't fix these one at a time, because for families they never arrive one at a time.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
